Under the bold statement "An AI agent will conduct and write research that is accepted by a technical conference such as NeurIPS within the next 5 years." it reads: Yann said, "False." I asked him 10 years? He said, "False". That is word for word what the candidate quotes.

The page is a blog post by Rajeev Chand, the moderator, dated "January 2025". In it he recalls the fireside chat he hosted at CES "yesterday", one prompt at a time. It is neither a transcript nor LeCun's own post. LeCun's only words on it are the single word "False", given through the moderator's account. So "coverage only" fits.

The page gives only "January 2025", not a day. 2025-01-07 is a reasonable inference: the page says Jensen Huang's statement was made at CES "the day before", and his keynote was on 6 January. Still, the exact day is not on the page.

**2. The four parts of the rule**

- **Part 2, looks forward and is about AI:** This passes. By answering "False" he forecasts that an AI agent will not produce research accepted at NeurIPS or a similar conference within 5 years, or within 10. Reading 2 counts a "will not happen by a date" forecast as a claim. The statement itself was the moderator's and LeCun only rejected it. That is the same set-up as the recorded "superintelligence-in-two-or-three-years-false" claim, so I don't treat it as a hypothetical.
- **Part 3, a date or span:** This passes: 5 years and 10 years from 2025-01-07. A person should decide whether this becomes one claim or two. The 10-year "not" implies the 5-year one, but the restatement rule doesn't cover two spans given in one breath.
- **Part 4, primary source:** This falls short. The only source is the moderator's write-up, not a recording or transcript, so it is a coverage-only entry.

**Already recorded?** No. None of his files covers an AI agent writing accepted research. The nearest dated files (2025-01-23, from Davos) are about other things.
